epics.name: Server foundations
epics.goal: The plumbing every later route leans on. Build it once, stop rewriting it.

epics.name: Data layer
epics.goal: Postgres, Drizzle and a schema that can answer the queries the chat list needs.

epics.name: Authentication
epics.goal: Hand-rolled JWT access and refresh tokens: the epic with the most to learn and the most to get wrong.

epics.name: People
epics.goal: Finding other humans, which every messaging feature after this depends on.

epics.name: Conversations
epics.goal: The chat list, which is a harder query than it looks.

epics.name: Messages
epics.goal: Sending, reading and paginating, all over plain HTTP before any socket is involved.

epics.name: Realtime
epics.goal: A raw ws server: rooms, heartbeats and reconnection are yours to build, which is the point.

epics.name: Attachments
epics.goal: Image messages, which the Conversation screen already renders.

epics.name: Hardening
epics.goal: The work that separates a demo from something you would leave running in public.

epics.name: Cut the client over
epics.goal: Retire mockData.ts. The screens are already built, so this is wiring rather than design.

milestones.name: A server you can test
milestones.outcome: Nothing user-facing yet. At the end you have a config that refuses to boot when it is wrong, one error shape, one way to validate input, and a test command that proves it.

milestones.name: Rows in Postgres
milestones.outcome: A database in Docker, the Drizzle migration loop you will repeat a dozen more times, and the first table.

milestones.name: You can sign in
milestones.outcome: Register, log in, refresh, log out, and a protected route that returns your own profile. The first milestone that feels like a real backend.

milestones.name: Two people can message each other
milestones.outcome: Find a user, open a DM, send messages, page back through history. No sockets anywhere yet, which is deliberate: get the write path right while it is still debuggable with curl.

milestones.name: The chat list works
milestones.outcome: Unread counts, read receipts, edits and deletes. CNV-2 is the hardest SQL in the project and it sits right here.

milestones.name: Messages arrive live
milestones.outcome: The whole realtime epic, plus the logging and shutdown work it leans on. Two browsers open, type in one, watch it land in the other.

milestones.name: Groups and images
milestones.outcome: The remaining screens you already designed: GroupInfo, and the image bubbles in Conversation.

milestones.name: The real client
milestones.outcome: mockData.ts is deleted. The React app you already built now runs on your own API.

milestones.name: Safe to leave running
milestones.outcome: Rate limits, browsable API docs, integration tests against a real database, and CI that blocks a broken branch.

milestones.name: Live at jchat.modularhq.app
milestones.outcome: Built, containerised, deployed, migrating on boot, with the WebSocket upgrade surviving the proxy.

tickets.title: Typed, validated environment config
tickets.what: Parse process.env through a zod schema at startup and export a frozen, typed config object. The process should refuse to boot with a readable message when DATABASE_URL or JWT_SECRET is missing, rather than failing later with undefined.
criteria: Booting without a required variable prints which key is missing and exits with code 1
No file outside config.ts reads process.env
Existing PORT, API_PREFIX and API_VERSION constants survive the rewrite
tickets.learn: Fail-fast configuration, and why a typed config module beats scattered process.env reads.

tickets.title: Standard error format and async error handling
tickets.what: An AppError class carrying an HTTP status and a machine-readable code, plus a terminal error middleware that renders every failure as { error: { code, message, details } }. Express 5 forwards rejected async handlers automatically, so no wrapper is needed.
criteria: Throwing new AppError(404, "chat_not_found", ...) returns that exact JSON shape
An unexpected throw returns a 500 with a generic message and never leaks a stack trace
Unknown routes hit a 404 handler that uses the same shape
tickets.learn: Express middleware ordering, and the difference between an operational error and a bug.

tickets.title: Request validation middleware
tickets.what: One validate(schema) middleware that checks body, params and query against zod schemas and replaces req values with the parsed output, so handlers receive typed, coerced data.
criteria: A bad payload returns 400 with a per-field details array
Handlers read parsed values with no casts and no any
Query numbers such as ?limit=20 arrive as numbers
tickets.learn: Parse, do not validate: pushing unknown input into typed shapes at the edge of the system.

tickets.title: Vitest and supertest harness
tickets.what: Split the Express app out of the listen call so tests can import the app directly. Add Vitest plus supertest and cover /health, a 404 and a thrown AppError.
criteria: pnpm test runs from the repo root and from apps/server
Tests import createApp() and never open a real port
Coverage reporting is wired even if the number is low at first
tickets.learn: Separating app construction from process startup, the single change that makes an Express codebase testable.

tickets.title: Postgres in Docker Compose with a pooled client
tickets.what: A compose file with a pinned Postgres image and a named volume, plus a pg Pool created once and exported. Wire a readiness check that runs SELECT 1.
criteria: docker compose up -d brings up a database the server can reach
The pool is created once per process, never per request
GET /api/v1/health reports database reachability
tickets.learn: Connection pooling, and why opening a connection per request destroys a Node server.

tickets.title: Drizzle Kit wiring and the migration loop
tickets.what: Install drizzle-orm and drizzle-kit, add drizzle.config.ts, and settle the loop you will repeat for every table: edit schema, generate SQL, review the SQL, apply. Add db:generate, db:migrate and db:studio scripts.
criteria: Generated SQL lands in a committed migrations folder and is reviewed before applying
Migrations apply cleanly against an empty database
The typed db client is exported from one module
tickets.learn: Why migrations are committed artifacts rather than something generated at deploy time.

tickets.title: users table
tickets.what: Columns for id (uuid), email (citext or lowercased with a unique index), password_hash, display_name, about, phone, avatar_color, created_at, updated_at. Add the timestamp defaults now so later tables copy the pattern.
criteria: Two users cannot register the same email in different cases
The Drizzle model infers a User type consumed by @jchat/shared
password_hash is never selectable through the shared public type
tickets.learn: Modelling identity, and keeping secret columns out of types that travel to the client.

tickets.title: Register with argon2 password hashing
tickets.what: POST /api/v1/auth/register hashes the password with argon2id and creates the user. Return the same generic response whether or not the email was taken, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts.
criteria: The stored hash includes its own salt and parameters
A weak or short password is rejected by the zod schema
Response time does not obviously differ for taken and free emails
tickets.learn: Why password hashing must be slow, and what a timing side channel gives away.

tickets.title: Login and access-token signing
tickets.what: POST /api/v1/auth/login verifies the password and returns a short-lived access token (roughly 15 minutes) in the JSON body, signed HS256 with a sub, iat and exp.
criteria: A wrong password and an unknown email return the same 401 body
The token payload carries no personal data beyond the user id
Token lifetime comes from config, not a literal
tickets.learn: What a JWT actually is: signed, not encrypted, and readable by anyone holding it.

tickets.title: requireAuth middleware
tickets.what: Read the bearer token, verify the signature and expiry, load the user id onto req.auth, and augment the Express Request type so downstream handlers see it without casting.
criteria: An expired token returns 401 with a distinct code from a malformed one
req.auth.userId is typed everywhere with no any
A protected route with no header never touches the database
tickets.learn: Declaration merging in TypeScript, the idiomatic way to extend Express types.

tickets.title: Refresh-token rotation with reuse detection
tickets.what: A refresh_tokens table storing hashed tokens with a family id. POST /auth/refresh issues a new pair and revokes the old token. Presenting an already-used token revokes the whole family, on the assumption it was stolen. Send the refresh token as an httpOnly, secure, sameSite cookie.
criteria: Refreshing twice with the same token logs the session out entirely
Refresh tokens are stored hashed, never in plaintext
The cookie is httpOnly and scoped to the refresh path only
tickets.learn: The whole reason refresh tokens exist, and why rotation without reuse detection buys you very little.

tickets.title: Logout and revoke every session
tickets.what: POST /auth/logout revokes the presented refresh token and clears the cookie. POST /auth/logout-all revokes every family for the user, which is what a Settings screen needs.
criteria: After logout the refresh token is rejected
The access token still works until it expires, and that is documented
logout-all requires a valid access token
tickets.learn: The core tradeoff of stateless tokens: you cannot un-issue one, only outlive it.

tickets.title: Profile read and update
tickets.what: GET /api/v1/me returns the signed-in user. PATCH /api/v1/me updates display name, about and avatar colour, mapping onto the fields the Settings and ContactProfile screens already render.
criteria: PATCH accepts a partial body and ignores unknown keys
Email and password are not editable here
The response uses the shared public user type
tickets.learn: PATCH semantics, and why partial updates need a different schema from creates.

tickets.title: conversations and conversation_members
tickets.milestoneName: Two people can message each other
tickets.what: A conversations table with kind (dm or group), name, description and pinned_message_id, and a conversation_members join table with role, joined_at and last_read_message_id. Composite primary key on (conversation_id, user_id).
criteria: A user cannot be added to the same conversation twice
Deleting a user cascades to their memberships
Group-only columns are nullable and documented as such
tickets.learn: Many-to-many modelling, and putting the state that belongs to a membership on the join table.

tickets.title: messages table and the pagination index
tickets.milestoneName: Two people can message each other
tickets.what: Columns for id, conversation_id, author_id, body, client_key, created_at, edited_at and deleted_at. Add the composite index on (conversation_id, created_at DESC, id DESC) that keyset pagination will use.
criteria: EXPLAIN on the history query shows an index scan, not a sequential scan
Deleting a conversation removes its messages
client_key is unique per author so retries cannot duplicate
tickets.learn: Reading an EXPLAIN plan, and designing the index alongside the query it serves.

tickets.title: Move initials and avatar colour into @jchat/shared
tickets.milestoneName: Two people can message each other
tickets.what: The client derives initials and an avatar colour from a name. Move that logic into the shared package so the server assigns the same colour at registration and both sides agree.
criteria: One function, imported by both apps
The colour is stable for a given user id
Unit tested in the shared package
tickets.learn: What actually belongs in a shared package in a monorepo, and what does not.

tickets.title: User directory search
tickets.milestoneName: Two people can message each other
tickets.what: GET /api/v1/users?q= returns users matching a name or email prefix, capped and excluding the caller. This backs the New Chat picker.
criteria: An empty or one-character query returns 400 rather than the whole table
Results are limited and never include email addresses of non-contacts
Search is case-insensitive
tickets.learn: Designing a search endpoint that cannot be used to scrape your user table.

tickets.title: Open or reopen a direct message
tickets.milestoneName: Two people can message each other
tickets.what: POST /api/v1/conversations/dm with a target user id returns the existing DM if one exists and creates it otherwise, inside a transaction so two fast taps cannot create two rooms.
criteria: Calling it twice returns the same conversation id
Concurrent calls do not produce duplicate DMs
Returns 201 on create and 200 on fetch
tickets.learn: Transactions and unique constraints as the real defence against a race, rather than a check-then-insert.

tickets.title: Fetch one conversation behind a membership guard
tickets.milestoneName: Two people can message each other
tickets.what: GET /api/v1/conversations/:id with a reusable requireMembership guard, since every message route needs the same check.
criteria: A non-member gets 404, not 403, so the endpoint does not confirm the room exists
The guard is one middleware reused by the message routes
The membership lookup is a single indexed query
tickets.learn: Authorisation as distinct from authentication, and when a 404 is the more secure answer.

tickets.title: Send a message over REST
tickets.milestoneName: Two people can message each other
tickets.what: POST /api/v1/conversations/:id/messages inserts the row and returns the created message with its server timestamp and id. Realtime comes later; get the write path correct first.
criteria: Empty or whitespace-only bodies are rejected
Body length is capped and the cap is in config
The response is the full message object the client can render immediately
tickets.learn: Why the server, never the client, owns ids and timestamps.

tickets.title: Idempotent sends with a client key
tickets.milestoneName: Two people can message each other
tickets.what: The client generates a uuid per message and sends it as client_key. A retry after a dropped response returns the original message instead of creating a second one.
criteria: Posting the same client_key twice returns the same message id
The unique constraint, not an application check, is what enforces it
A duplicate returns 200 while a fresh send returns 201
tickets.learn: Idempotency keys, the standard answer to at-least-once delivery over an unreliable network.

tickets.title: Cursor-paginated history
tickets.milestoneName: Two people can message each other
tickets.what: GET /conversations/:id/messages?before=<cursor>&limit=50 returning newest first with an opaque cursor built from (created_at, id). Not OFFSET, which drifts as new messages arrive.
criteria: Paging back through a conversation while new messages land never skips or repeats a row
The cursor is opaque to the client and validated on the way in
The query uses the DB-5 index
tickets.learn: Keyset versus offset pagination, and why every chat app in the world uses keyset.

tickets.title: Seed script from the web mock data
tickets.milestoneName: Two people can message each other
tickets.what: Port the four contacts and their chats out of the client mock into a seed script, so a fresh database gives you the same screens you already designed against.
criteria: pnpm db:seed is idempotent and safe to run twice
Every seeded account shares one known development password
The seed refuses to run against a non-local DATABASE_URL
tickets.learn: Seed data as a development tool, and guarding destructive scripts against the wrong environment.

tickets.title: Conversation list with last message and unread count
tickets.what: GET /api/v1/conversations returns every conversation the caller belongs to with its latest message, the other member for DMs, and a count of messages after the caller last_read_message_id. Sorted by latest activity. This is the ChatList screen in one request.
criteria: One round trip to Postgres, not one query per conversation
A conversation with no messages still appears
The response maps cleanly onto the existing Chat type
tickets.learn: The N+1 query problem, lateral joins and window functions. The single most valuable SQL ticket here.

tickets.title: Edit and soft-delete
tickets.what: PATCH and DELETE on a message, author-only. Deletion sets deleted_at and blanks the body rather than removing the row, so pagination cursors and reply references survive.
criteria: Editing someone else message returns 403
A deleted message still occupies its position in the timeline
edited_at is set and surfaced in the response
tickets.learn: Soft deletes, and the query discipline they demand everywhere afterwards.

tickets.title: Read receipts and unread counts
tickets.what: POST /conversations/:id/read with the last message id the user has seen, advancing conversation_members.last_read_message_id and never moving it backwards. Unread counts derive from it.
criteria: Marking an older message as read does not decrease the pointer
Unread counts in the list endpoint match what the conversation shows
A user own messages never count as unread
tickets.learn: Monotonic state, and storing a pointer instead of a row per message per reader.

tickets.title: Contacts add, remove and list
tickets.what: A contacts table (owner_id, contact_id, created_at) plus endpoints to list, add and remove. Decide deliberately whether contacts are one-directional, and write the decision down.
criteria: Adding the same contact twice is a no-op, not an error
You cannot add yourself
The list returns the fields ContactProfile renders
tickets.learn: Idempotent writes, and why PUT-like behaviour is friendlier than a 409 here.

tickets.title: Structured logging with request ids
tickets.what: Add pino and pino-http. Attach a request id to every inbound request, log method, path, status and duration, and pretty-print in development only.
criteria: Every log line in production is a single JSON object
The same request id appears on the access log line and on any error logged from that request
Passwords and tokens are redacted
tickets.learn: Why structured logs beat console.log once something is deployed and you cannot attach a debugger.

tickets.title: Graceful shutdown
tickets.what: On SIGTERM and SIGINT: stop accepting connections, let in-flight requests finish, close the database pool, then exit. Force-exit after a timeout so a stuck socket cannot hang a deploy.
criteria: Ctrl+C during an in-flight request lets that request complete
The process exits within the timeout even with an open connection
Shutdown reason and duration are logged
tickets.learn: The Node process lifecycle, and why a container platform sends SIGTERM before SIGKILL.

tickets.title: Attach a ws server and authenticate the upgrade
tickets.what: Create the WebSocketServer with noServer: true and handle the HTTP upgrade event yourself, verifying the access token before completing the handshake. Reject unauthenticated upgrades with 401 rather than accepting and closing.
criteria: An upgrade with no valid token never becomes an open socket
The authenticated user id is attached to the socket
The ws server shuts down with the HTTP server from FND-6
tickets.learn: How a WebSocket connection begins life as an HTTP request, and where you get to intervene.

tickets.title: Typed socket protocol in @jchat/shared
tickets.what: A discriminated union of client-to-server and server-to-client frames, each with a type field, defined once in the shared package and parsed with zod on receipt. Version the protocol from the start.
criteria: Both apps import the same frame types
An unknown or malformed frame is logged and ignored, never crashing the connection
Switching on frame.type narrows exhaustively in TypeScript
tickets.learn: Discriminated unions and exhaustiveness checking, TypeScript at its most useful.

tickets.title: Connection registry and per-conversation fan-out
tickets.what: A Map from user id to their open sockets (a user has several tabs), and a publish(conversationId, frame) that looks up members and writes to each of their sockets. Membership decides delivery, so no client can subscribe its way into a room.
criteria: A user with three tabs receives the message on all three
A non-member never receives a frame for that conversation
Closed sockets are removed from the registry on close and on error
tickets.learn: Server-side subscription state, and why the server rather than the client decides who is in a room.

tickets.title: Heartbeats and dead-socket reaping
tickets.what: A ping on an interval with an isAlive flag cleared on each ping and set on pong. Terminate sockets that miss a round. Without this, half-open connections accumulate until the process runs out of memory.
criteria: Killing a client at the network level frees its registry entry within one interval
The interval is cleared on shutdown so tests do not hang
terminate is used for dead sockets, close for clean ones
tickets.learn: Why TCP will not tell you a peer is gone, and what a half-open connection costs.

tickets.title: Broadcast sends, edits and receipts
tickets.what: Have the message service publish after a successful commit, so a socket frame never announces a write that rolled back. The REST endpoints stay as they are and gain a broadcast.
criteria: A failed insert broadcasts nothing
The sender other tabs receive the message too
The frame payload is the same object the REST response returns
tickets.learn: Ordering side effects after a transaction commits, and the dual-write problem this avoids.

tickets.title: Typing indicators
tickets.what: A client typing frame that fans out to the other members and is never persisted. Throttle on the client, expire on the server after a few seconds of silence.
criteria: Nothing about typing is written to Postgres
The indicator clears on its own if the sender disappears
Your own typing frame is not echoed back to you
tickets.learn: Ephemeral state, and recognising the data that must never touch a database.

tickets.title: Presence and last seen
tickets.what: Derive online from the registry rather than a column: a user is online while they hold at least one socket. Write last_seen_at on the last disconnect. This backs the online dot in ChatList and ContactProfile.
criteria: Closing one of three tabs leaves the user online
A crash still results in offline once the heartbeat reaps the socket
Presence changes fan out only to that user contacts
tickets.learn: Derived state over stored state, and why an is_online column always drifts out of date.

tickets.title: Reconnect and catch-up
tickets.what: The client reconnects with exponential backoff and jitter, sending the last message id it holds per conversation. The server replies with everything since, so a tunnel or a sleeping laptop does not lose messages.
criteria: Killing the server and restarting it restores a live client with no gap
Backoff has jitter, so a restart does not stampede every client at once
Catch-up reuses the MSG-2 pagination path rather than a second code path
tickets.learn: At-least-once delivery over an unreliable transport, the problem Socket.IO would have hidden from you.

tickets.title: Create a group and manage its members
tickets.what: POST /conversations/groups with a name and member ids, plus endpoints to add and remove members. The creator becomes the first admin.
criteria: Only an admin can add or remove members
An admin cannot remove the last admin
Leaving a group you are not in returns 404
tickets.learn: Role checks that live in the service layer rather than being scattered across handlers.

tickets.title: Group metadata and admin actions
tickets.what: PATCH the group name and description, promote and demote admins. Backs the GroupInfo screen.
criteria: Every mutation emits an event the realtime epic can broadcast later
Changes are validated for length and trimmed
Non-admins receive 403 with a clear code
tickets.learn: Designing service functions that return a result plus the events to publish.

tickets.title: Pin a message
tickets.what: Set and clear conversations.pinned_message_id, validating that the message belongs to that conversation. The Conversation screen already renders a pinned banner.
criteria: Pinning a message from another conversation is rejected
Unpinning clears the column
Deleting the pinned message clears the pin
tickets.learn: Referential integrity you have to enforce yourself when a foreign key alone is not enough.

tickets.title: Image upload with real validation
tickets.what: POST /api/v1/uploads accepting one image behind multer, with a size cap and a content type checked from the file magic bytes rather than the client-supplied header. Store on disk behind an interface you can swap for object storage later.
criteria: A renamed .exe is rejected despite claiming image/png
Oversized uploads are rejected before the whole body is buffered
The storage adapter is an interface with a local implementation
tickets.learn: Streams and multipart parsing, and why a Content-Type header is a claim rather than a fact.

tickets.title: Attach media to a message and serve it
tickets.what: An attachments table linked to messages, plus a download route that checks conversation membership before serving bytes. Caption and dimensions travel with the message.
criteria: A non-member cannot fetch the file even with the exact URL
Responses carry cache headers and an accurate content type
An orphaned upload is cleaned up or expires
tickets.learn: Authorising static assets, the step people skip when they hand out unguessable URLs.

tickets.title: API client and token storage
tickets.what: A small typed fetch wrapper that attaches the access token, refreshes once on a 401 and replays the original request, queueing concurrent calls so a burst triggers one refresh rather than five.
criteria: Three simultaneous 401s cause exactly one refresh call
The access token lives in memory, not localStorage
A failed refresh routes to the login screen once
tickets.learn: Why an access token in localStorage is an XSS liability, and the memory plus httpOnly-cookie pattern instead.

tickets.title: Login and register screens
tickets.what: Two screens in the existing visual language, plus a session boot that attempts a silent refresh on load so a returning user is not asked to log in again.
criteria: Server error codes map to field-level messages
The app shows a loading state during the silent refresh rather than flashing the login screen
Forms are keyboard and screen-reader usable
tickets.learn: Auth as an application state machine: unknown, authenticated, anonymous.

tickets.title: Replace mockData with server queries
tickets.what: Add TanStack Query and swap chats, contacts, getChat and getContact for real requests, one screen at a time. Delete mockData.ts last, once nothing imports it.
criteria: Every screen handles loading, empty and error states
Message history pages in on scroll using the MSG-2 cursor
mockData.ts is deleted and the build still passes
tickets.learn: Server state versus client state, and why a query cache is not the same thing as a store.

tickets.title: Live socket hook and optimistic send
tickets.what: A useSocket hook owning one connection for the app, pushing incoming frames into the query cache. Sending renders the message immediately with its client key and reconciles when the server frame arrives.
criteria: A message sent in one browser appears in another within a second
An optimistic message is replaced, not duplicated, when its server copy lands
A failed send is marked as failed and can be retried
tickets.learn: Optimistic UI and reconciliation by client key, which is exactly what MSG-3 was built for.

tickets.title: Security headers, CORS and body limits
tickets.what: helmet for headers, a cors policy that allows the Vite origin with credentials in development and nothing cross-origin in production (same origin there), and an explicit express.json size limit.
criteria: The dev client can call the API with cookies attached
An oversized JSON body is rejected with 413 in the standard error shape
Production responses carry the helmet defaults
tickets.learn: What CORS actually gates, and why credentials change the rules.

tickets.title: Rate limiting
tickets.what: A global limit plus a much tighter one on login, register and refresh, keyed by IP and by account. Return 429 with Retry-After in the standard error shape.
criteria: Repeated failed logins for one account are throttled regardless of source IP
Limits are configurable and disabled in tests
The limiter store survives a restart, or its loss is a documented tradeoff
tickets.learn: Credential stuffing as the actual threat, and why IP-only limiting does not stop it.

tickets.title: OpenAPI spec and browsable docs
tickets.what: Generate the OpenAPI document from the zod schemas you already wrote, and serve it with Scalar at /api/docs in development. Keep the existing Bruno collection in sync.
criteria: The spec is generated from the schemas, never hand-maintained
Every endpoint documents its error codes
Docs are not exposed in production unless deliberately enabled
tickets.learn: Single-sourcing validation and documentation so they cannot disagree.

tickets.title: Integration tests against a real Postgres
tickets.what: Run the suite against a throwaway database, migrating before and truncating between tests. Cover the auth flow end to end, the conversation list query and message pagination.
criteria: The suite passes from a clean checkout with only docker compose up
Tests are order-independent
The realtime path has at least one test with two real socket clients
tickets.learn: Testing against the real database rather than mocks, and where each approach earns its place.

tickets.title: GitHub Actions CI
tickets.what: A workflow running lint, typecheck, test and build on every push, with a Postgres service container and a pnpm store cache.
criteria: A failing test blocks the branch
Installs are cached so the run stays under a couple of minutes
The workflow uses the same Node version as production
tickets.learn: Service containers in CI, and keeping the pipeline fast enough that you do not learn to ignore it.

tickets.title: Serve the built SPA from Express
tickets.what: In production, serve apps/web/dist as static files and add a catch-all that returns index.html for non-API paths, so client-side routes survive a refresh. The dev Vite proxy already imitates this.
criteria: A hard refresh on a deep link returns the app, not a 404
The catch-all never swallows /api routes
Hashed assets get long cache headers and index.html gets none
tickets.learn: Single-origin deployment, which removes the CORS and cookie problems rather than solving them.

tickets.title: Multi-stage Dockerfile
tickets.what: Build the workspace with pnpm in one stage and copy only the production output into a slim runtime stage running as a non-root user.
criteria: The final image carries no dev dependencies or source maps you did not intend
Layer order means a code change does not reinstall dependencies
The container runs as a non-root user
tickets.learn: Image layers and build caching, and why the naive Dockerfile is enormous and slow.

tickets.title: Deploy to jchat.modularhq.app
tickets.what: Pick a host, provision managed Postgres, set secrets, point the subdomain, terminate TLS and confirm the WebSocket upgrade survives the proxy, which is the step that usually breaks.
criteria: wss:// connects through the production proxy and stays open past any idle timeout
Secrets live in the platform, never in the repo
A push to main results in a deployed change with no manual steps
tickets.learn: Reverse proxies and WebSocket upgrade headers, plus TLS termination in practice.

tickets.title: Migrations on boot and a real readiness probe
tickets.what: Run pending migrations at startup behind a lock so two instances cannot race, and split liveness (the process is up) from readiness (database reachable, migrations applied).
criteria: Two instances starting together apply each migration exactly once
The platform routes traffic only after readiness passes
A failed migration stops the deploy instead of serving a broken build
tickets.learn: Advisory locks, and the difference between liveness and readiness that every orchestrator assumes you know.
